description: Scan a repository for proper nouns an STT engine is likely to mangle: package and dependency names, git authors, README brands, the project directory. Only names the repo says somewhere other than its own source are proposed: a class that exists nowhere but code is something the user types, not something they say, and adding it teaches the lexicon to rewrite ordinary dictation. WHEN TO CALL: when you are in a repo with no .lexicon.yaml and the user dictates about it, or when they ask what this project would add. Call it without `add` first -- that is a read-only preview. WHAT IT CHANGES: nothing unless `add: true`, which writes the candidates into the repo's .lexicon.yaml. Show the candidate list and get a yes first. A file the user already trusted stays trusted; a new, untrusted or changed one is not trusted by the write (`trusted: false`) and applies only after the user reviews it and runs `lexicon trust` (or `npx @ashlr/lexicon trust`): relay `nextStep`. `path` must be inside the server directory, its git root, a client root or LEXICON_HARVEST_ROOTS; anything else is refused, and so is `add: true` when the .lexicon.yaml it would write (found by walking up from `path`, or new at its git root) is outside them and not this server's own project file. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: it does not touch the global lexicon, and it does not pull file contents into the conversation -- candidates come back as names, categories and counts: { root, candidates: [{ canonical, category, source, evidence, count, suggestedAliases }], count }, plus `truncated: true` and a `note` when the scan stopped at its file cap (tell the user, and offer to harvest a subdirectory), where `evidence` names where a name was seen (a file path, "git log", "package.json#name"), never the text around it, and `suggestedAliases` is often empty on purpose (an identifier gets none). With `add: true` the result adds `added`, `failures` and `path`, and is an error when no candidate could be written.

add.description: When true, add every candidate to the project lexicon. A file that is not trusted yet is left untrusted for the user to review.

limit.description: Max candidates to return (default 50, at most 1000).

minCount.description: Minimum occurrences for a name found only in file text (default 2). The directory name, git authors, package names and dot-TLD brands (Ashlr.AI) are proposed at any count.

path.description: Repository root. Omit for the server working directory (a blank one is refused). Must be inside it, its git root, a client root or LEXICON_HARVEST_ROOTS.

name: harvest_repo
title: Harvest names from a repository
